_schema.what: One verdict per SKILL GROUP (a rank ladder; ranks share prose). Keyed by group id, which is the skill id with its rank digit removed.
_schema.why: 14,410 skill rows collapse to 2,684 groups, 2,246 of them cast-facing, and until 2026-09-12 a human had read about 21. There was no ORACLE: the only way to answer 'does this skill do what its prose says' was to play it on a phone, which is how every defect this project has found was actually found. These verdicts are that oracle.
_schema.no_pack_text: Reasons are written in English and describe the clause; they never quote _note1. The pack's own text stays out of git (CLAUDE.md section 10) -- tools/skill_review.py prints it into an untracked worksheet instead.

status.ok: every clause in the prose is represented, with the right number, recipient and gate
status.partial: the main effect is right; a secondary clause or a gate is missing
status.broken: a clause is wrong, lost, duplicated, or fires when it should not
status.suspect: looks wrong but needs a second reading or a device check

classes.missing_gate: the clause states a condition and the effect compiles ungated, so it always fires
classes.wrong_recipient: lands on the wrong side or the wrong subset
classes.duplicate_effect: one clause compiled into two effects
classes.lost_clause: a stated effect produced nothing at all
classes.glossary_leak: a status's own description compiled as a skill effect
classes.wrong_language: the number came from the English where the Chinese states a different one (section 3)
classes.unresolved_category: a cleanse or gate carries a category nothing can match
classes.missing_chance: the clause states odds and the effect is certain
classes.lost_stacks: a stated stack count is not represented

_schema.reviewed_by: read from the Chinese prose against the compiled effects via tools/skill_review.py
